"""A lending shelf: copies go out to borrowers and come back.

A copy is either on the shelf or on loan to exactly one borrower. A loan is never
edited; returning a copy ends its loan. Overdue is a question asked of a loan at a
given day, so the shelf keeps no clock of its own.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Loan:
    copy_id: str
    borrower: str
    due_day: int

    def overdue(self, today):
        return today > self.due_day


class Shelf:
    def __init__(self, copy_ids):
        self._available = set(copy_ids)
        self._loans = {}

    def lend(self, copy_id, borrower, due_day):
        if copy_id not in self._available:
            raise ValueError('that copy is not on the shelf')
        self._available.remove(copy_id)
        loan = Loan(copy_id, borrower, due_day)
        self._loans[copy_id] = loan
        return loan

    def give_back(self, copy_id):
        loan = self._loans.pop(copy_id)
        self._available.add(copy_id)
        return loan

    def overdue_loans(self, today):
        return sorted((loan for loan in self._loans.values() if loan.overdue(today)),
                      key=lambda loan: loan.due_day)
